title: G 500 4×4²
verdict: A G-Class on stilts: portal axles, two springs per corner and 22-inch wheels. Utterly unsubtle — but the 17 inches of ground clearance are entirely real.

paragraphs: The 4×4² — say it “four-by-four squared” — is what happened when Mercedes took the running gear of its six-wheeled G 63 AMG 6×6, removed an entire axle and bolted the result under an ordinary long-wheelbase G. The result stands 88 inches tall, clears 17.2 inches of rock and wades through 39.4 inches of water. Mercedes-Benz USA called it the most capable G-Class ever, and charged $225,000 to prove it.

story.heading: FROM SIX WHEELS TO FOUR
paragraphs: It started as a show car. At the Geneva Motor Show in March 2015 Mercedes displayed the G 500 4×4² with no commitment to build it, saying production would depend on the reaction. The reaction was enthusiastic, and Mercedes put it into production in 2015. Underneath it is the body of the five-door long-wheelbase W463 on a shortened version of the 6×6’s chassis.

The trick is the portal axle. A gear drop at each hub puts the wheel centre below the axle tube, so the diffs and axle housings ride far higher than on a normal G — 450 mm (17.7 in) of ground clearance in European spec, against 9.3 inches for a standard [[g-class/g550|G 550]]. The track grew too, by 299 mm, filled out with detachable carbon-fibre wheel-arch flares and 325/55R22 tires. For the 2017 model year the truck came to America as the G 550 4×4², at $225,000 plus destination.

story.heading: TWO SPRINGS PER CORNER
paragraphs: Each wheel gets two spring struts in parallel — one with fixed damping, one adjustable — and Mercedes claimed the switch between Comfort and Sport took 15 milliseconds. Two stabilizer bars help keep it upright, and the drivetrain is pure G: permanent four-wheel drive split 50:50, a low-range transfer case and three 100% differential locks. Power came from the 4.0-litre twin-turbo M176 V8, rated 416 hp and 450 lb-ft in the US, driving through a seven-speed automatic.

Mercedes first showed the idea as a concept nicknamed “Extreme-G”. According to Car and Driver's prototype drive, cited by Wikipedia, the G-Class had sold more than 14,000 units in 2014, and that demand freed up budget for low-volume spin-offs like this one. KW developed the dual-strut suspension, and the truck could reach 60 mph in under six seconds. On paper it beat the Hummer H1 in almost every off-road measurement. The exception was side slope: it was limited to a 28.4° bank angle against the Humvee's 30°.

Mercedes-Benz USA’s numbers are absurd in the best way: 51.6° approach, 43.8° departure, a breakover of 44.6° at maximum load in the spec sheet (47.4° in the launch release), 69-inch-plus track widths, a 46.9-foot turning circle and a 6,694-lb curb weight. It returned 11 mpg city, highway and combined, according to the same sheet. Expedition Portal, not given to gushing about concept trucks, said Mercedes had knocked it “straight out of the park.”

story.heading: THE END, AND WHAT CAME NEXT
paragraphs: With the [[g-class/second-gen|second-generation G]] due in 2018, Mercedes announced it would stop taking 4×4² orders at the end of October; in Germany it had cost €231,693. Its portal axles and raised suspension lived on in the Mercedes-Maybach G 650 Landaulet, and in 2022 the idea returned as the G 63 4×4² — now with independent front suspension, 585 hp and a $350,050 sticker, and 379 lb lighter than the old truck.

Today the original is a collector’s off-roader that people actually use. Bring a Trailer regularly lists them — one 2017 G 550 4×4² with 39k miles came on Pirelli Scorpion ATRs, with plugs, a coil and transmission service in its records — and shops now build lookalikes: Houston’s Banyan Motors converted a 2000 [[g-class/g500|G 500]] with a LeTech dual-suspension setup, portal axles and beadlocks. Rivals? Nothing from the factory, though the [[land-rover/defender-l663|new Defender]] and [[grenadier/station-wagon|Grenadier]] owners will happily argue.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · BY THE NUMBERS
callout.title: 4×4² versus a 2016 G 550
paragraphs: Ground clearance: 17.2 in vs 9.3 in. Wading depth: 39.4 in vs 23.6 in. Approach angle: 51.6° vs 30°. Departure: 43.8° vs 30°. Height: 88.0 in vs 76.9 in. Curb weight: 6,694 lb vs 5,724 lb. Price: $225,000 vs $119,900.

Same engine, same seven-speed, same three lockers and the same 112.2-inch wheelbase. Almost everything that changed is in the running gear — which is precisely where off-roaders want it to change. (All figures from Mercedes-Benz USA.)

engineering_intro: The 4×4² keeps the G-Class fundamentals — ladder frame, rigid axles front and rear, full-time four-wheel drive and three lockers — and changes the geometry around them. Portal hubs lift the axle housings; a wider track and dual-spring suspension keep the tall truck stable. Mercedes-Benz USA noted that the portal design let it leave suspension geometry, steering links and driveshafts essentially unchanged from other G-Class models while reducing driveshaft load.

engineering.note: Shortened version of the G 63 AMG 6×6’s chassis under a long-wheelbase W463 body.
Longitudinal and transverse links front and rear; hub reduction gears drop the wheel centre below the axle.
Two struts per wheel; Comfort/Sport switching claimed at 15 ms. Two stabilizer bars.
Low-range transfer case; 7G-TRONIC PLUS seven-speed automatic.
Three 100% locks, engaged on the move.
Approach and departure. 17.24 in clearance at max load, 39.4 in fording (MBUSA).

engineering_note.title: WHY PORTAL AXLES
engineering_note.body: On a normal axle the differential sits level with the wheel centre, so the diff housing is the lowest thing under the truck. Portal hubs add a gear set at each wheel that moves the drive down to a lower hub, raising the whole axle — and buying ground clearance without a giant lift or ever-bigger tires. The cost is weight, complexity and more gears to service.

buying_checks.head: Make sure it’s a real one
buying_checks.body: Shops build 4×4² lookalikes from ordinary Gs — some, like Banyan Motors’ portal-axle G 500, are serious builds, but they aren’t factory trucks. Confirm the VIN, window sticker and data card.

buying_checks.head: Price the tires before the truck
buying_checks.body: Factory fitment is 325/55R22 on 9.5×22 wheels — big, heavy and not cheap. Check tread depth and date codes, and whether the spare matches.

buying_checks.head: Test the adjustable dampers
buying_checks.body: Switch between Comfort and Sport on the drive. You should feel the difference immediately; a fault light or no change means a damper or control problem.

buying_checks.head: Test all three lockers
buying_checks.body: Engage centre, rear and front on a loose surface and watch the indicators. Trucks that never left pavement often have lazy lockers.

buying_checks.head: Inspect the carbon flares and roof
buying_checks.body: The detachable carbon-fibre arch extensions and roof-mounted lights live high and wide — look for cracks, chips and scratches (one BaT example noted roof scratches).

buying_checks.head: Ask for the service file
buying_checks.body: Spark plugs, ignition coils, transmission fluid and filter, brake fluid — the BaT example’s history shows the kind of records to expect. Ask specifically about portal-hub and axle oil changes.

buying_checks.head: Measure your garage
buying_checks.body: It’s 88 inches tall and 86.2 inches wide with mirrors. Parking structures and automatic car washes are now hostile territory.

buying_checks.head: Rust where nobody cleans
buying_checks.body: It’s still a W463: check the tailgate lower edge, door bottoms, sills, rear frame tubes and strut mounts.

repairs.title: Spark plugs & ignition coils (M176)
repairs.symptoms: Misfire codes, rough idle, hesitation under load. Plugs are a scheduled item; coils fail individually.
repairs.fix: Remove the engine covers, unplug and pull each coil, and replace the plugs with the correct Mercedes-spec part, torqued to spec. Swap any coil that misfire data points to — or move coils between cylinders to confirm before buying.
repairs.tools: Mercedes-spec spark plugs · ignition coil(s) as needed · thin-wall spark-plug socket and extensions · torque wrench · scan tool

repairs.title: Seven-speed fluid & filter service
repairs.symptoms: Harsh or slurred shifts, or simply no record of a service. The 7G-TRONIC has no dipstick, so fluid level is set by temperature.
repairs.fix: Drain the pan, replace the filter and pan gasket, refill with the Mercedes-approved fluid, then set the level at the specified temperature using a scan tool to read transmission temperature.
repairs.tools: Filter and gasket kit · MB-approved ATF · fill adapter/pump · scan tool for fluid temperature · torque wrench
know: PistonHeads says broken integrated speed sensors on the 7G-TRONIC (from 2003) cause random shifting or no shifting, so a truck that shifts erratically may need more than a fluid change.
mistakes: Blaming old fluid for erratic shifts without scanning for speed-sensor faults.

refs.name: PistonHeads: Mercedes G-Class (W463) PH used buying guide

repairs.title: Diff locks won’t engage
repairs.symptoms: A lock refuses to engage or drops out; indicator lights flash. On W463s the cause is usually actuation — vacuum or wiring — rather than the differential.
repairs.fix: Work the system from the actuator back: confirm vacuum or signal at each lock, then trace lines and connectors toward the source with a gauge or meter. Fix the leak, then exercise the locks regularly. PistonHeads warns that G-Class diffs can seize if they're rarely used, so exercise the locks rather than leaving them for an emergency. PistonHeads gives a diff oil change every 40,000 km (≈25,000 mi) with heavy off-road use, or every 60,000 km (≈37,000 mi) on a mainly on-road truck.
repairs.tools: Hand vacuum pump with gauge · multimeter · vacuum tees and line · replacement connectors

parts.name: Vacuum hoses listed for the G 550

know: On the 4x4² the portal hubs carry their own oil; datbananaguy on MBWorld changes it every 30,000 km (owner figure).

refs.name: PistonHeads: Mercedes G-Class (W463) PH used buying guide
MBWorld: G550 4x4 squared trade value & maintenance (owner thread)

repairs.title: Steering damper & wander
repairs.symptoms: Wander, wheel shake at highway speed, vague on-centre feel, clunks — amplified by tall tires and a rigid front axle.
repairs.fix: Replace the steering damper with an OEM or upgraded unit, check drag link and tie-rod ends for play, then align. The 4×4² keeps the G’s steering linkage, so the usual W463 diagnosis applies.
repairs.tools: Steering damper · sockets and wrenches · tie-rod or drag-link ends if worn
know: An MBWorld member puts damper life at around 70,000–80,000 miles; others have replaced leaking ones under warranty at under 10,000.
A road-force tire balance (under 20 lb, one member suggests) often cures a 60 mph shake that gets blamed on the damper; the damper slows steering response, it doesn't fix vibration.
Tire pressure matters: one owner noticed the wobble less once the tires were warm and at the right pressure.
mistakes: Fitting a stiffer damper to mask an out-of-balance tire or worn joints.
Ignoring an oily damper body, the sign it has started to leak.

repairs.title: Sunroof drains & water ingress
repairs.symptoms: Damp or sagging headliner, wet carpets, electrical gremlins.
repairs.fix: Clear all four sunroof drains, then check the headliner, fuse box and climate actuators for water damage.
repairs.tools: Trimmer line or drain-cleaning wire · low-pressure air · towels
know: The sunroof tray has a drain tube at each corner. On the W463 the front tubes run down the A-pillars and the rear ones down the back, and they exit low on the body. One MBWorld member says the front tubes end near the rocker panels.

Blocked drains aren't the only way water gets in. MBWorld owners also point at wiper-pivot seals, the windshield gasket, the roof antenna base, door seals and a hole in the right-side firewall under the battery box.
A tube can break or come off its spigot behind the headliner. That needs the headliner dropped, not just a clean.
Water that sits in the footwells reaches wiring and modules under the carpet, so dry the floor fully and check connectors as soon as you find it.
mistakes: Blowing high-pressure air into the drains, which can knock the tube off inside the pillar.
Assuming it's the drains and missing a wiper-pivot, antenna or firewall leak.
Leaving wet carpet in place, where it soaks the wiring underneath.
Forcing a stiff wire down a tube and puncturing it.

refs.name: MBWorld: Passenger floor board soaking wet (W463)

repairs.cost_note: Clearing the drains costs nothing but time. Dropping the headliner to reattach a tube is a few hours of careful work. The expensive part is what water damages if it's left: wiring, modules and a stained headliner.

repairs.title: Frame & body rust treatment
repairs.symptoms: Bubbling at the tailgate lower edge, door bottoms and sills; scale on the rear frame tubes and strut mounts.
repairs.fix: Wire-brush or blast back to sound metal, treat and paint, or cut in repair panels where needed. Inject cavity wax into doors and frame rails, keep drain paths clear and wash off road salt after winter. PistonHeads suggests checking the online MOT history first for "vehicle structure is corroded" comments, then inspecting the underside for rock damage and the tailgate and the areas around the back lights.
repairs.tools: Wire wheels or blaster · rust converter and primer · cavity wax with extension wand · welder for panel repairs

parts.name: Eastwood Internal Frame Coating (cavity wax for frame rails)

know: PistonHeads says rust was a much bigger problem on pre-1991 G's; on a 2015–2018 truck look hardest at rock damage underneath.
EuroAutoPro notes that rock chips can lead to rust around the wheel arches and lower panels.

refs.name: PistonHeads: Mercedes G-Class (W463) PH used buying guide
EuroAutoPro: Common problems of the G 500 4x4²

repairs.title: Brake booster vacuum hose recall (17V-817)
repairs.time: Minutes to check. Dealer visit for the fix.
repairs.symptoms: A hard brake pedal that needs more effort than usual to stop the truck. The booster's vacuum hose can collapse.
repairs.fix: NHTSA recall 17V-817 covers 432 model-year 2017 G 550 and G 550 4×4² trucks. The brake-booster vacuum hose may collapse and raise braking effort, and dealers replace the hose as needed for free. Run the VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls before you buy, and ask for the paperwork if it's been done. On a 6,694-lb truck, this is not one to put off.
know: Recall 17V-817 covers 2017 G 550 and G 550 4x4² models built from April 3 to May 31, 2017: 432 trucks in the US, 100 of them 4x4². Mercedes estimated 1% actually had the defect.
Daimler said the brake booster vacuum hose may not have been made to production specification and could delaminate and partly or fully collapse.
With less vacuum, the brakes need more pedal effort, which raises crash risk depending on traffic.
The remedy is free at a Mercedes-Benz dealer: they check the hose and replace it if needed.
mistakes: Assuming a used 4x4² has had it done; check the VIN on NHTSA.
Living with a hard pedal instead of getting the hose checked.
repairs.cost_note: Free at a dealer under the recall.

refs.name: NHTSA: recall 17V-817 defect report (G 550 and G 550 4x4² brake booster vacuum hose)

repairs.title: Oil leaks from the crankcase vent oil separators (M176)
repairs.time: Separators: a few hours. Rear main seal: transmission out (shop job).
repairs.cost: Rear main seal: about $5 in parts but $3,000–5,000 in labor (Handsome Motors)
repairs.symptoms: Oil seeping from the valve covers or from where the engine meets the transmission, a burning-oil smell, and oil consumption between changes.
repairs.fix: Handsome Motors, which has owned more than 200 Gs, says the 2016–2018 G 550's M176 suffers rear main seal and valve cover gasket leaks triggered by a failed crankcase-vent oil separator. The 4×4² uses the same engine. Fix the cause first by replacing the left and right oil separators, which FCP Euro lists for the G 550 4×4², and then deal with any valve cover leaks. A rear main seal leak means removing the transmission. Handsome Motors also suggests 3,000–5,000-mile oil changes on these engines.
repairs.tools: Socket set · torque wrench · trim tools for the engine covers · new seals and gaskets

parts.name: Genuine Mercedes crankcase vent valve / oil separator, left 177 010 79 03 (G 550 4×4²)
Genuine Mercedes crankcase vent valve / oil separator, right 177 010 80 03 (G 550 4×4²)
Genuine Mercedes rear crankshaft seal with flange 177 010 03 00 (G 550, G 550 4×4)
Valve cover gaskets listed for the G 550

repairs.title: Leaking adjustable dampers
repairs.cost: Dealer quote $3,500 for one rear side (one owner)
repairs.symptoms: Oil wetting the body of a shock, a bouncier ride, or a damper fault on the dash. On MBWorld, efathalla says the rear shock on his 2017 4x4² (about 14,000 miles) leaked, and the original poster in the same thread listed leaky shocks among his worries before buying.
repairs.fix: Clean the damper bodies and drive a few miles to see which one is weeping. A damper that's damp with road film but not dripping can be watched; one that is running oil or has lost damping needs replacing, ideally in axle pairs. The 4x4²'s adjustable dampers are specific to the truck, so get the part through a Mercedes dealer or a G specialist by VIN, and don't fit a standard G-Class shock. efathalla says the dealer quoted "$3500.00 for one side"; he skipped the repair and reported no problems for about a year afterwards, which tells you a slow weep isn't an emergency, not that it can be ignored for ever.
repairs.tools: Jack and axle stands · wheel chocks · torque wrench · the workshop manual for the damper connector and mounts
know: PistonHeads says W463 springs break, especially at the rear and after heavy off-road use, so check the springs while the damper is out.
The same MBWorld owner reported more wind noise than a standard G and about 11 mpg, so budget accordingly.
mistakes: Fitting a standard G-Class shock to a 4x4².
Replacing one damper and leaving a tired one on the other side.
repairs.cost_note: The only figure we found is the single-owner dealer quote above; independent shops may be cheaper.

refs.name: MBWorld: G550 4x4 squared trade value & maintenance (owner thread)
PistonHeads: Mercedes G-Class (W463) PH used buying guide

repairs.title: Portal axle oil leaks and oil changes
repairs.symptoms: Oil weeping from a portal hub housing at one wheel, or oil flung onto the inside of the wheel. On MBWorld, ThreeGs says the only maintenance issue on his 2017 4x4² at about 33,000 miles was a fluid leak from a portal axle.
repairs.fix: Clean the hub housing and recheck after a drive to find the source: a weep from a drain or fill plug usually just needs a new sealing washer, while oil from the hub seal or the housing joint means a seal job. Check the oil level in every portal hub, not only the leaking one. For routine changes, datbananaguy says the 4x4² needs the same maintenance as a G 500/G 550 plus a portal axle oil change every 30,000 km (about 18,750 miles); that's an owner's figure, so confirm the interval and oil spec with a dealer or the maintenance booklet for your VIN.
repairs.tools: Drain pan · the correct fill-plug socket or hex · fluid pump · new plug washers
know: After deep water, check the hub oil for a milky colour; water in the oil means a seal or vent problem.
PistonHeads gives a diff oil change every 40,000 km (≈25,000 mi) with heavy off-road use, or every 60,000 km (≈37,000 mi) on a mainly on-road truck.
mistakes: Topping up one hub and not checking the other three.
Using an oil that isn't to the spec in the booklet for your VIN.

refs.name: MBWorld: G550 4x4 squared trade value & maintenance (owner thread)
PistonHeads: Mercedes G-Class (W463) PH used buying guide

repairs.title: Cruise-control recall 17V-713 (ESP software)
repairs.symptoms: None in normal driving. DealerRater's recall list says a fault in the Electronic Stability Program while Distronic Plus is engaged may keep the engine from reducing power. The recall covers 2016–2017 G 550 4Matic, G 63 AMG and G 65 AMG vehicles.
repairs.fix: Run the VIN through a recall lookup or ask a Mercedes dealer whether campaign 17V-713 (Mercedes 2017110012) has been done. The remedy is a free reprogramming of the ESP control unit by dealers, which began on December 6, 2017. Ask for a printout showing it's complete before you buy.
know: The 2017 4x4² also has the brake booster vacuum hose recall (17V-817); see our separate guide.
DealerRater also lists two 2021 eCall recalls for 2016–2021 Mercedes models, both fixed free by software or by activating the communication module.
mistakes: Assuming an imported or grey-market truck has had its recalls done.
repairs.cost_note: Recall work is free at a Mercedes dealer.

refs.name: CarComplaints: recall 17V-713, cruise control may not disengage

faq.q: What’s the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: It doesn't need one — the portal axles are the lift. Stock tires are 325/55R22, about 36 inches tall. When Mercedes showed the truck, it said 37×12.5×18 mud-terrains would be available for production trucks, and its concept photos showed 37-inch mud-terrains on beadlocks. Mercedes-Benz USA says larger off-road tires can be fitted without recalibrating the speedometer, because it reads from the axles. Check caliper clearance before going to 18-inch wheels.

faq.q: Was the 4×4² sold in the US?
faq.a: Yes, for the 2017 model year, as the G 550 4×4². Mercedes-Benz USA listed it at $225,000 plus a $925 destination charge, with deliveries from early 2017.

faq.q: How much ground clearance and wading depth?
faq.a: 17.24 inches at maximum load and 39.4 inches of fording depth in US spec — up 7.9 and 15.8 inches respectively over a 2016 G 550. European figures are 450 mm and 1,000 mm.

faq.q: What are its approach and departure angles?
faq.a: 51.6° approach and 43.8° departure. Mercedes quoted breakover as 47.4° in its launch release and 44.6° at maximum load in the spec sheet.

faq.q: Is it just a G 63 6×6 with an axle missing?
faq.a: Partly. It uses a shortened version of the 6×6’s chassis and portal running gear, but with the five-door long-wheelbase body, the G 500/G 550’s 4.0-litre twin-turbo V8 and a seven-speed automatic.

faq.q: What fuel economy does it get?
faq.a: Mercedes-Benz USA’s spec sheet lists 11 mpg city, 11 highway and 11 combined. The fuel tank holds 25.4 gallons.

faq.q: Will it fit in my garage?
faq.a: Maybe not. It’s 88.0 inches tall, 86.2 inches wide including mirrors and 177.1 inches long, with a 46.9-foot turning circle.
6,694 lb curb weight — almost a thousand pounds more than a regular G 550.
Mercedes-Benz USA’s 2017 spec sheet listed towing as “TBA,” so check the owner’s manual and hitch rating for your specific truck rather than assuming the regular G 550’s figure.

faq.q: Can I use the diff locks on pavement?
faq.a: No. Locked diffs bind the driveline on grippy surfaces. Lock up on loose ground at low speed and unlock before tarmac.

faq.q: How is it different from the newer G 63 4×4²?
faq.a: The 2022-on G 63 4×4² is built on the second-generation G with independent front suspension, makes 585 hp and costs $350,050. It has less clearance (13.8 in) and wading depth (35.8 in) than the original, and weighs 379 lb less.

mods.why: Brabus’ Adventure package is designed specifically for the 4×4² — bodywork, lighting and off-road upgrades.
Long-wheelbase W463 racks fit the 4×4² body — though at 88 inches tall, loading the roof is a ladder job.
Turning a show-pony 4×4² into a self-sufficient travel truck: storage, power, lighting, recovery.
Can’t find a factory truck? Builders add portal axles and dual suspension to ordinary W463s — Banyan Motors’ LeTech-equipped G 500 is one example.
Dropping from 22s to 18-inch beadlocks with 37-inch mud-terrains is the classic 4×4² move — verify caliper clearance first.

baseline_service.intro: The 4×4² shares its engine, gearbox and lockers with the 2016–2018 G 550, so the drivetrain basics are the same — but the portal axles add hub reduction gears that a regular G doesn’t have, and many shops have never serviced one. Baseline everything, and confirm portal-axle specs with a Mercedes dealer.

items.note: The 2018 manual, which also covers the 4×4², lists MB 229.5 for all models. FCP Euro lists its 9-litre 229.52 kit and the Mann filter kit for the G 550 4×4². Check that whatever oil you use carries an approval your manual allows.

Check every hub for weeps and compare the oil from each corner. A dealer that has done one before is worth finding.
